purpose: R2 of the BEN-157 repair: ONE treatment for the receipt-trust items (audit items 2, 3, 4, 5). R3 and R4 remain unapplied; promotion remains BLOCKED.
authorization: Repair authorized by the mediator after codex's part 7. Conditions honoured: tests land in the same commit, NOTHING deployed to scratch, CODE_ROOT untouched, campaign not re-run.
THE_ONE_INVARIANT_R2_ENCODES: Every quantity the reconciler checks is derived from the filesystem at CANONICAL paths and from constants pinned in the tool -- never from the receipt's account of itself. Four reported defects were four faces of that; they are fixed as one change rather than four patches, which is the mediator's point that seven patches would leave an eighth.

WHAT_CHANGED.item_3_canonical_artifact_path: The training stage hashed `art['path']` straight from the receipt, compared against nothing. It now hashes os.path.join(d, TRAIN_ARTIFACT_NAME) and adds `artifact_path_is_canonical`, testing the receipt's path claim against the launcher's name. The TARGET stage already did exactly this at :324; the training stage did not, in the same file I wrote.
WHAT_CHANGED.item_2_training_stage_markers: The target stage read two .done sentinels and the training stage read none. It now checks the weights marker and the training receipt's own marker.
WHAT_CHANGED.item_4_the_primitive_is_CALLED_not_reimp: The hand-rolled `done_*` size comparison is replaced by a call to atomic_write.is_complete, which compares size AND mtime. One retained hand-rolled check, `..._marker_names_current_subject`, ADDS what is_complete cannot do: is_complete derives the marker path from the subject, so a marker copied from another replica with matching size and mtime would satisfy it.
WHAT_CHANGED.item_5_all_three_code_digests: The tool read `head_at_runtime` (itself a CLAIM in the receipt, not a measurement) plus one loader sha, while the producer records THREE digests and the launcher checks all three. Now: each of the three is required present, each is re-hashed from its recorded path when that path resolves, and all three digests AND paths must be constant across the family.
WHAT_CHANGED.why_family_constancy_rather_than_a_pin: The two driver digests FLOAT BY DESIGN -- they ride the next launch with a CODE_ROOT sync (OI-57/OI-58) -- so pinning a value would be wrong. Constancy across members catches a driver that changed MID-FLIGHT, which is exactly what a floating pin leaves open and what no pinned constant could detect, because a pin matches every member equally.
WHAT_CHANGED.naming_discipline: `code_<role>_matches_disk` is deliberately NOT `code_<role>_is_the_right_driver`. It proves the file at a recorded path now matches its record; it does not prove the path is the right one. BEN-149's lesson applied to a check I was writing.

A_FAIL_LOUD_IMPORT_AND_A_NEW_DEPLOYMENT_.what: The tool now imports atomic_write. It is deployed to scratch as a SINGLE script, so the tempting fallback is 'if atomic_write is missing, do the size-only check'.
A_FAIL_LOUD_IMPORT_AND_A_NEW_DEPLOYMENT_.why_that_fallback_is_refused: That fallback IS the defect item 4 recorded. A missing primitive means the tool cannot perform the check it claims, so it exits 3 with a message naming the file to copy rather than silently downgrading to a weaker gate.
A_FAIL_LOUD_IMPORT_AND_A_NEW_DEPLOYMENT_.CONSEQUENCE_FOR_OI_64: Deployment must now copy atomic_write.py alongside reconcile_gate5_family.py. This is a NEW constraint created by R2 and it belongs in the re-deployment step, not discovered during it.

WHAT_I_DELIBERATELY_DID_NOT_ADD.completion_marker_valid: Codex reported that a receipt declaring itself invalid passes. True, but the sharper form is that NO receipt from this producer CAN declare itself invalid: `train_fullevent_replica.py:358` writes the Python literal True. Requiring it would be A CHECK THAT CANNOT FAIL -- the class this entire repair is about -- so it is not read as evidence. I drafted exactly that check and removed it before running anything; the measurement it gestures at is `weights_marker_is_complete`. Vocabulary defect filed as OI-66.

TWO_DEFECTS_I_INTRODUCED_AND_THE_SECOND_.1_fixture_could_not_satisfy_both_the_pin: My first fixture gave the loader a real stub file AND claimed EXPECTED_LOADER_SHA, which no stub can do without a sha256 preimage, so `code_loader_matches_disk` failed. Resolved by pointing the loader at an absent path -- the disk re-hash skips for that role and the pinned `loader_sha256` covers it -- rather than monkeypatching the pin, which would hide it. Real receipts satisfy both because the real loader genuinely hashes to the pin, and that is confirmed below.

2_A_FAMILY_INVARIANT_THAT_COULD_NOT_FAIL.what: I put the training code digests at the row's top level. `constant_across_family` reads `row['invariants']`, so EVERY member resolved to None, producing ONE group -- indistinguishable from unanimous agreement. The invariant certified the family while measuring nothing.
2_A_FAMILY_INVARIANT_THAT_COULD_NOT_FAIL.how_it_was_caught: By its own power test. `test_a_driver_that_changed_MID_FAMILY_is_caught` failed because the family invariant never fired; only the per-member check did. Had I written the positive half alone, this would have shipped as a green check.
2_A_FAMILY_INVARIANT_THAT_COULD_NOT_FAIL.the_wider_fix: `constant_across_family` now also returns whether the path RESOLVED, and both invariant loops assert it. A misspelled or misplaced path previously certified the family silently -- that latent trap covered the twelve pre-existing target invariants too, not just my new ones.

VERIFIED_AGAINST_THE_LIVE_FAMILY_BEFORE_.why: Fixtures prove the logic; they do not prove R2 is DEPLOYABLE. If production receipts disagreed with any new assumption, R2 would fail all 50 members and block the campaign it exists to certify. Checked read-only, nothing deployed.
VERIFIED_AGAINST_THE_LIVE_FAMILY_BEFORE_.artifact_path_is_canonical: Real receipt records the canonical path exactly. PASSES.
VERIFIED_AGAINST_THE_LIVE_FAMILY_BEFORE_.training_stage_markers_exist_in_producti: Both GATE5_REPLICA_WEIGHTS.npz.done and GATE5_REPLICA_TRAINING_RECEIPT.json.done are present on disk. The producer always wrote them; the RECONCILER never read them and the FIXTURE never created them. Item 2 was a verifier gap, not a producer gap.
VERIFIED_AGAINST_THE_LIVE_FAMILY_BEFORE_.all_three_code_paths_resolve: All three point into GATE5_CODE_ROOT and are readable, so `code_*_matches_disk` runs for all three in production -- including the loader, unlike the fixture.
VERIFIED_AGAINST_THE_LIVE_FAMILY_BEFORE_.is_complete_accepts_every_real_marker: 150 subjects checked (25 weights + 25 training receipts + 50 target npy + 50 target receipts): is_complete FALSE for 0. Production markers carry `mtime`, so delegating to the primitive does NOT reject the live family.
VERIFIED_AGAINST_THE_LIVE_FAMILY_BEFORE_.reading: R2 is safe to deploy. Had any of these four been false, the correct move would have been to hold R2, not to weaken it.

INCIDENTAL_OBSERVATION_not_filed_as_new: A real weights marker's note reads `gate4 fullevent nominal tag=nominal` and its `job` field is the per-task allocation id, not the array id. The note is OI-61's `--tag nominal` mislabel surfacing inside a product rather than only in a receipt field. Cosmetic, already owned by OI-61, recorded so the next reader does not re-derive it.

TESTS.positive_half: The 90 pre-existing tests are the positive half: every R2 check passes on a clean fixture, which is what makes them checks rather than alarms.
power_tests_added: test_a_receipt_AGREEING_with_a_wrongly_named_artifact_now_fails -- codex's attack verbatim; an exact PASS before R2
test_marker_check_catches_an_MTIME_only_change_which_the_old_hand_rolled_one_could_not -- THE proof of delegation: size untouched, mtime moved 100 s, so the old size-only check would pass
test_a_driver_that_changed_MID_FAMILY_is_caught -- every member internally consistent, disagreeing with each other
fixture_defects_repaired_in_the_same_com: Markers were hand-written with output/size/marked_at and NO mtime, which is why the suite never exercised the mtime axis and why is_complete rejected fixture markers for reasons unrelated to any probe. Now written by the real atomic_write.mark_complete.
The training stage created NO .done markers -- codex's part-7 observation and the direct reason item 2 was invisible here.
The `code` block carried digests with no `path`, so the new disk re-hash would silently skip on every fixture. Two roles now have real stub files.
